x: Eric, married to Mavis, daughter of past President of the Club, Tom Morrell, now lives in Cheshire. So great is his enthusiasm for Belgrave and competition that he still travels down regularly to compete, and he tells me, to chat over tactics and walking generally over a cup of tea in 'Joe Lyons's'…

Mavis, Hannah and Neil seem to have adapted to the way of life, which admittedly is more comfortable and relaxing. We have more time together as a family and, talking of families, we are expecting an increase in June!
John has now moved to Winnipeg and we wish him, Mavis and their children the best of luck in their new home. If anyone wishes to write to John his new address is [address withheld].
He was also a great help on the social scene and was a fine fellow who will be missed by all who knew him. Our deepest sympathy to his wife Mavis and family.

Mavis is particularly cross with you for suggesting that you could still find a place for me in a Belgrave team!! I have started training but as I met with an accident after my first outing up in York she was not best pleased - nor were the NHS!
We send our condolences to Tom's widow Rose, and to Mavis, Eric and all of Tom's family.

There are not too many Belgravians I suspect who were as closely questioned by him as I was when Mavis and I started going out together! I was also confused at that time as he was always known as Uncle Jerry in the Morrell household and with his approaches to me I thought he was part of the family a…

No expense spared I was told and so Mavis came as navigator, interpreter and general factotum. The starting point was Sydney and we were soon made aware of the importance of the year 2000 to the residents.

During two days spent in the library and studios Mavis and I were able to relive our visit to Rome in 1960; see the Melbourne footage of my own and Stan's events, plus we had time to look through Games reports produced by the host cities and other National Olympic Committees.
Top right: Mavis cycles behind Herne Hill's Ron Clarke in a race at Walton - 1954 or 55?.
But going back for a moment to his earlier days with the Club; perhaps emboldened by his success at athletics, Race Walker Eric set himself another target - the winning of young Mavis.
